summary.headline: Premier Explosives Q2 FY27 revenue rose 92% YoY to Rs 1,452.8 mn and EBITDA rose 161% YoY to Rs 172.3 mn, with order book at Rs 16,420 mn.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations recovered sharply from a weak Q1 that was hit by dispatch and project delays linked to global headwinds and supply chain disruptions. EBITDA margin widened to 11.9% from 8.7% a year earlier and 5.7% in Q1. H1 FY27 profitability fell year on year, with EBITDA down 15.9% and PAT down 54.8%. Management said the order book stood at Rs 16,420 mn as of October 2026, about 96% defense. Q&A was dominated by export licence delays, the RDX/HMX capacity ramp, margin pressure, and the Apollo Micro Systems transaction.

segments.name: Defense
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 96% of the Rs 16,420 mn order book. Export RDX/HMX and shafts/flares work is tied to export licences.

segments.name: Explosives services / bulk explosives
segments.commentary: Remainder of the order book (~4%). Management expects about Rs 80 mn of bulk explosives revenue this year from the existing Singareni order; no new bids named.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the revenue recovery momentum to continue; H2 revenue of about Rs 300 cr was implied by an analyst and not contradicted, based on the countermeasures order balance of about Rs 270 cr expected to complete before March 2027.
Kakinada-type RDX/HMX plant: commercial production targeted by mid-to-end December 2026; initial Q4 FY27 output around 30 tonnes with about Rs 20 cr revenue potential.
FY28 RDX/HMX target of about 300 tonnes, at a blended realisation of USD 60-80 per tonne, with 50-60% consumed internally; subject to export licences.
Export licence for the Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) expected 'next month', but timing is not in management's control.
Shafts and flares expected to contribute about Rs 200 cr of revenue in FY27 based on current orders.
capex_capacity: RDX/HMX capacity being raised from 100 tpa to 600 tpa; commissioning targeted by the end of this financial year.
H1 FY27 capex was about Rs 11 cr against an earlier plan of about Rs 32 cr for FY27; the shortfall is expected to be spent in H2 on the RDX/HMX project and logistics.
Mine programme: Nippon Mines order in hand; Roshi and Ulka are in qualification. Order size mentioned as more than Rs 2 lakh pieces (transcript unclear); value not disclosed.
Drone payloads are in armed forces qualification and currently supplied on trial basis in small quantities; volume not quantified.
40 mm grenade ammunition: stalled, dependent on imported propellants and primers from MIL, which are unavailable.
No plans to set up 155 mm artillery shell facility.
demand_pricing: Countermeasures order (Jul 2023, ~Rs 75 cr): delivery period extension from the government expected in the current quarter; about Rs 30 cr receivable pending on this order.
Countermeasures order (Oct 2025, Rs 430 cr): about Rs 110 cr executed by H1; balance about Rs 270 cr expected to complete before March 2027.
Export orders: licence process takes 3-4 months after buyer end-user certificates are submitted to MoD and DGTR (transcribed as DVP); applications are made order by order, not product by product.
RDX/HMX international prices described as fluid; demand exceeds supply in both domestic and export markets.

Gross margin on defense mixture supply has declined from about 42% in FY26 (as stated by analyst) to lower levels, attributed to a long-term 10-11 year fixed-price contract, imported Flare components after an accident at the Flare plant last year, and supply chain delays. Management said commercial-segment margins should target at least 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Has the delivery period extension on the Jul 2023 countermeasures order (Rs 75 cr) been received, and when will the balance be completed?
qa_highlights.answer: Extension expected this quarter; supplies are continuing. Completion about three months after extension. About Rs 30 cr receivable pending.

qa_highlights.question: When will the export licence for the Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is in final stages and could come next month, but declined to give a precise timeline, saying it depends on government and committee approval.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be new bulk explosives orders from Singareni or Coal India subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Singareni extended the existing contract and supplies continue; expected about Rs 80 cr of bulk explosives revenue this year. Future growth depends on Singareni's new RFP.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RDX/HMX revenue potential in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 300 tonnes output at USD 60-80 per tonne blended realisation, with 50-60% consumed internally. Depends on export licences.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Apollo acquisition expected to change governance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said governance is expected to remain the same for now and did not comment further.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AP land status?
qa_highlights.answer: The state government has formulated a defense and ammunition industry policy; the company selected one of four options. A board reconstitution is expected by December 2026 in connection with the Apollo transaction.

risks_watch: Export licence timelines (3-4 months per order after end-user documents) are outside management control and have delayed revenue.
Gross margin compression from fixed-price long-term contracts, imported components and supply chain delays.
RDX/HMX commissioning timeline (December 2026) and ramp-up; capex execution lagged plan in H1.
Dependence on MIL for propellants and primers for the 40 mm ammunition programme.
Apollo Micro Systems acquisition of an additional 41.33% stake and board reconstitution expected by December 2026.
Management did not disclose the Rs value of the mine order or the composition of the order book between propellants and rocket motors.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q2 operating recovery and order book, but cautious and at times evasive on export licence timing, order-level margins, and product-level revenue potential, which management repeatedly deferred to government approvals.
key_quotes: I am pleased to share that Q2 marked a strong recovery in our operating performance with improved business momentum translating into significant revenue growth and better operating profitability.
The defense segment accounts for nearly 96% of the total order book providing strong revenue visibility for the coming periods.
This is not in our hands. It is the government policy based on that and then the committee has to approve that.

adds.what: RDX/HMX capacity raised from 100 tpa to 600 tpa (Kakinada-type plant), initial Q4 FY27 output ~30 tonnes

growth.why: Management expects revenue recovery momentum to continue, backed by a Rs 16,420 mn order book (96% defense), Rs 270 cr countermeasures balance due before March 2027, and shafts/flares guidance of Rs 200 cr in FY27, though export licence timing is outside management's control and RDX/HMX capacity ramp starts only from Dec 2026.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 11.9% from 5.7% in Q1 and 8.7% a year ago, but H1 margin of 9.3% is below 12.6% in H1 FY26 and gross margin on defense supply fell from about 42% in FY26 on fixed-price contracts and imported flare components; management targets at least 20% only for commercial segment.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: RDX/HMX capacity is being raised from 100 tpa to 600 tpa with commercial production targeted mid-to-end December 2026 and initial Q4 FY27 output of about 30 tonnes; H1 capex of Rs 11 cr against Rs 32 cr plan shows execution lag.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of Rs 16,420 mn (96% defense), Rs 270 cr countermeasures balance due before March 2027, and shafts/flares guidance of about Rs 200 cr in FY27 support volume recovery, though export licence timing (3-4 months per order) is outside management control and H1 revenue rose only 13.8% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: H1 capex was about Rs 11 cr versus Rs 32 cr FY27 plan with the shortfall to be spent in H2 on RDX/HMX and logistics; no new capex program was named, and management said no plans for a 155 mm shell facility.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided shafts/flares about Rs 200 cr, bulk explosives about Rs 80 cr and countermeasures balance about Rs 270 cr for FY27, but H1 PAT fell 54.8% and export licence timing is uncontrolled, so no upward revision is evident.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export licence for the Apr-2026 LV order (~Rs 50 cr) is pending with no firm timeline, the 40 mm ammunition programme is stalled on unavailable MIL propellants, and the RDX/HMX ramp starts only from December 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Drone payloads are in armed forces qualification on trial supply with volume unquantified, and RDX/HMX output starts at about 30 tonnes in Q4 FY27; the 40 mm grenade programme is stalled.

rows.label: Countermeasures order balance execution
rows.why: About Rs 270 cr of the Rs 430 cr Oct 2025 countermeasures order is expected to complete before March 2027, after about Rs 110 cr executed in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Export RDX/HMX and LV export licences
rows.why: Apr-2026 LV export order (~Rs 50 cr) licence is in final stages and could come next month, but management declined a precise timeline; FY28 RDX/HMX target of about 300 tonnes at USD 60-80 per tonne depends on licences.

rows.label: Apollo Micro Systems stake and board reconstitution
rows.why: Apollo is acquiring an additional 41.33% stake with board reconstitution expected by December 2026, though management said governance will remain the same for now.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 recovery, order book and RDX/HMX commissioning, but cautious and evasive on export licence timing, order-level margins and product-level revenue potential; analysts probed licence delays, the RDX/HMX ramp, margin pressure and the Apollo transaction.
